messages:
sam: thinking about adding a per-route cost preview panel in console — show expected unit-cost delta if we change routing policy for a tenant. quick mock: https://img.redwood/mock/routing-cost-preview :eyes:
neha: love it. should the preview simulate cache hit-rate changes too? prefetch/shared-cache effects swing unit costs a lot.
mia: agree but be careful. previews that assume warmed caches are misleading. propose two modes: steady-state (post-warm) and cold-start (first N requests) so customers see a range.
nashley: +1 for ranges. UX Q: where does this live? rollout page or quota/route editor?
sam: small panel on rollout page and a toggle in quota/route editor — same backend calc. show per-token, per-invocation, and amortized cost.
leo: backend note: to simulate accurately we need recent prefix-shape distribution and our cache crediting model. plan: run a lightweight sampling job over tenant last 7 days. estimate = baseline_unit_cost * routing_multiplier - cache_savings_estimate.
neha: cache_savings_estimate requires attributing prefix hits to routes. current telemetry tags only have model_name and route_id, not routing_decision. we should add token-level tags: routing_decision and cache_hit:true/false.
ops-bot: deploy queued: add-telemetry-routing-decision -> infra/staging (ETA 18:00)
mia: API sketch: POST /api/v1/preview/routing-cost {"route_from":"r1","route_to":"r2","window_days":7,"mode":"steady|cold"} -> {"token_cost":"...","cache_savings":"...","per_model_breakdown":[...]} keep it minimal.
neha: per_model_breakdown must include model_sku and quant_profile or numbers are useless.
ashley: product question for @product-lily — will customers grok amortized vs marginal? default to "expected per-invocation" with tooltip.
product-lily: i'll draft microcopy. include an example line: "Switching 10% of traffic to model-x lowers avg cost by 3% but increases p99 latency by 20ms" makes tradeoffs tangible.
sam: also show a diff: QPS redistribution, top-3 routes impacted, and expected change to cache hit-rate.
leo: tagging every token increases cardinality. suggestion: only tag sampled requests used by preview job; rest keep low-card metrics. sampling job should be deterministic by tenant so previews are stable.
neha: sampling fine but misses rare expensive prompt-shapes. UI should show a confidence band and sample coverage percent.
mia: +1 for confidence band and an "include shared-cache effects" checkbox with short explanation: "Estimates assume shared prefix cache is split proportionally across routes." be explicit.
ashley: rollout plan: dev -> staging -> canary with a few large tenants. add "preview-as" feature so SRE/product can run preview for tenant X before toggling routing.
leo: infra work: endpoints + background job to recalc previews daily for tenants with frequent config changes. store last_preview_ts and sample_coverage.
neha: i'll own QA for cache attribution accuracy and run a staged A/B: run preview then do a small controlled reroute and compare predicted vs observed costs.
ashley: finance wants CSV export with per-model/unit econ. they love spreadsheets :moneybag:. include per_model_line and total_impact columns.
sam: dev tasks: 1) add telemetry tags (routing_decision, cache_hit) 2) preview API + sampling job 3) UI panel + microcopy 4) canary + release notes. timeline?
leo: (1)+(2) ~2 sprints. sampling infra mostly exists.
mia: UI mock in 1 sprint. canary + docs next sprint.
neha: QA checks and A/B validation in parallel with canary. will produce a short report.
product-lily: i'll coordinate microcopy + legal on disclaimer. add a small "expected variance: +/- X%" line.
sam: good. i'll file RFC and tasks. tagging: @product-lily for microcopy, @leo for infra, @neha for QA. :thumbsup:
